styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Castle, old town lanes and the Danube's Cold War edge.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Pub plates, dumplings and riverside wine bars.

styles.label: Budget
styles.blurb: Cheap trams, cheap beer and a very walkable centre.

stays.why: Walk to the castle, the main square and most sights. Best for first-time visitors who want everything on foot.
Quiet evenings by the water, close to the UFO bridge and the Devín ferry. A short walk or tram to the old town.
Cheapest beds and big apartment blocks south of the river. Good tram links; plain but practical.
Local, residential and near the main train station. Good value if you arrive by rail and don't mind a walk.

food: Try Slovak classics: bryndzové halušky (potato dumplings with sheep cheese), kapustnica soup and lokše pancakes.
Pub lunches in the old town are good value; a main course often costs around EUR 8–14.
Look for a weekend 'street food' market or the old market hall for cheap local bites; check opening days on the day.
Wine bars serve Slovak and small-region wines; a glass is often a few euros. Ask for a local Frankovka or Veltlín.
Beer is cheaper than coffee in many places. A half-litre of local draft is often around EUR 2–3.
more_time: Take the Danube ferry to Devín castle in season for ruins and river views; check sailing times on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for a wine afternoon in the Small Carpathians; buses and trains reach the wine towns.
Cross to Austria by ferry in season for a half-day on the other bank; bring your passport.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the castle, old town and riverside at an easy pace; add a third for a Danube or wine day.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 4°C and lows around -2°C. Pack a warm coat; expect about 10 rain days.
February: still cold, highs near 8°C. Fewer tourists and lower prices.
March: milder at around 11°C, with about 7 rain days, the driest month.
April: spring arrives, highs near 16°C. Good for walking; keep a light rain layer.
May: pleasant at around 20°C but about 11 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
June: warm at around 26°C, with about 11 rain days. Long evenings outdoors.
July: the hottest month, highs near 28°C. Go sightseeing early; about 8 rain days.
August: hot at around 28°C and busy. Book hotels ahead.
September: warm at around 22°C and a good balance of sun and showers.
October: cooler at around 16°C; autumn colours along the river.
November: chilly at around 10°C with about 9 rain days. Pack layers.
December: cold at around 5°C. Christmas markets make the old town lively; bring gloves.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate: cold winters, warm summers and rain spread through the year.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs from about 20°C to 28°C. Comfortable for walking the old town and castle.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 4–8°C and lows near or below freezing. Warm coat, hat and gloves needed.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 7–11 rain days every month. May and June are the wettest; March the driest.

items.title: Sunny summers
items.text: July and August reach about 28°C with around 8 rain days. Long daylight hours.

items.title: Mild shoulder months
items.text: April and October sit around 16°C, good for sightseeing with fewer crowds.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers and a waterproof jacket any month; a warm coat for winter; light clothes and sunscreen for summer.

transit.best: Walk the centre; use trams for longer hops and ride apps for the airport.

modes.text: No metro in Bratislava. Don't plan around rail inside the city.
Bus 61 links the airport to the main train station; N61 runs at night. Buy tickets from machines before boarding.
Trams and trolleybuses cover the centre. Buy tickets from machines before boarding.
Uber, Bolt, Hopin and Liftago work reliably. Airport taxis are pricey; use an app instead.
Driving is easy, but parking in the old town is scarce and costly.
The centre is very walkable. Bikes are fine along the Danube.
A ferry runs on the Danube to Devín and across to Austria in season.
